fullGrain
Scannned images of grain. See the [?] button below for how to create these images.
frame range
Copy mask to the output mask.a channel

low_clip
Sets a low threshold, based on the input image, below which the grain will not be subtracted.
Use this channel from the original input to mix the output with the original input.
If the mask input is connected, use this channel from it to mix the output with the original input.

minwidth
Don't put grain on the image if it is less than this many pixels wide
Dissolve between the original image at 0 and the full effect at 1.

offset
Color of neutral gray to subtract from images

resize
Resizes the grain plate to match your input. If this is not checked, the grain is cropped to match.

saturation
Color saturation of the grain

A different pattern is produced for each frame. Change this number to get a different initial pattern, for instance if you have multiple Grain operators. If you require an identical grain plate for every frame, enter @i;-frame@n; in this field.
Image is divided by this channel before being processed, and multiplied again afterwards. This can improve color corrections of anti-aliased edges.
use precomputed table between 0 and 1.0 for faster processing. The table is clamped at 0.0 and 1.0.
The current pixel is looked up here to get a multiplying factor for the grain.

description.plain_text: Applies actual scans of film grain to replicate the grain of the scanned film stock. Random frames selected from a loop of scanned film grain is applied to the input image using an additive process To create the film grain images, film a grey card and scan the result in. Then blur this image and subtract it from the original, then add .5 to the rgb channels, and then save as a @i;raw@n; image. Only about 50 frames are needed.
